6.1.1 A short RL primer
Assume that we have an agent in an unknown environment, and that the agent can
interact with the environment and potentially obtain rewards based on its actions. In
reinforcement learning, we would like the agent to learn to maximize its cumulative
reward from its interaction with the environment. This means that the agent should learn
a strategy that allows it to adapt to its environment in order to maximize its reward. In
Go, this could mean train the agent to win as many games as possible, or in MRI, this
could amount to selecting the next line to acquire to maximize the reconstruction quality.
